title: Use cases supported by Personalisation Hub
summary: The 3 primary use cases — connected retail experience, first-party retail media targeting and hyper-localised QSR campaigns — with links to the articles that set each up.
bodyMd:
Personalisation Hub supports 3 primary use cases: a connected and personalised retail experience, first-party data targeting for retail media, and hyper-localised campaigns for quick-service restaurants. This page describes each scenario and links to the articles that set it up. For the sector view, see Benefits by industry.

Core platform features

All 3 use cases build on the same features. The platform runs entirely within your own AWS account and private VPC — see Where is my data stored and how is the platform secured?.

  • Retail data management — 1 record per store for hours, address, segments and enabled features, maintained by HQ and store staff. See How store data works in Personalisation Hub.
  • Virtual queue management — visitors queue digitally instead of standing in line. See Queue Management.
  • Appointment bookings — customers book a pickup or service time. See Appointment Bookings.
  • Digital signage — self-hosted, secure in-store displays on your own domain, capable of 1:1 personalisation. See Displays & Devices and Digital Signage & Campaigns.
  • Mobile store sites, QR Control, the Visitor API, AI agents and proximity — see Mobile Store Sites and Personalisation & AI.

Use case 1: connected and personalised retail experience

Applies to telco, banking and brick-and-mortar retail. The visitor's phone, the store's displays and the staff tablet are connected for the duration of the visit.

Virtual queues and appointments

  • Visitors check in on arrival and join a virtual queue, or arrive for a booked appointment. See Let a visitor join the queue by scanning a QR code on a display and Enable appointment bookings.
  • Joining the queue is the point at which the brand asks for consent to personalise the visit.
  • Customer data is aggregated from your CDP, CRM, AI/ML models and Amazon services through the Visitor API. See Connect your mobile app or third-party system to the Visitor API.
  • Visitors remain free to browse while they wait; SMS tells them when it is their turn. See SMS and email messages sent to visitors.

Connected customer journeys

  • A unified profile personalises digital signage and staff-tablet campaigns. See Use customer and decisioning data to personalise the store visit.
  • Shared displays show content based on the store section, or 1:1 based on the proximity of a known customer. See Enable proximity personalisation with MIST.
  • First-party cookies on your primary domain personalise displays for prospects the platform has not identified.
  • The reasons visitors are waiting in the queue guide what the store's displays play. See Localise campaigns by visitors' reason for visit.

Dynamic QR code engagement

  • QR codes on displays let a visitor check in and be personalised immediately. See Enable QR Control and set the default QR code settings.
  • A scanned code surfaces the customer's history for targeted campaigns.
  • QR Control turns the visitor's phone into a remote control for the display. See What are triggered campaigns?.
  • Visitors browse offers on the mobile store site and act on a call to action. See Create a call to action for on-rotation campaigns.
  • The platform can also drive AR or mixed-reality experiences such as a personalised magic mirror.

Staff tablet

  • Store managers monitor every visit in progress from the tablet. See View store queueing stats and the staff status widget.
  • Customer information surfaces when staff pick a visitor from the queue. See View a visitor's recent interactions and profile data.
  • Staff can play a triggered campaign on a display while talking to the visitor. See Let retail staff activate triggered campaigns.
  • Interaction data feeds back into the visitor's profile and into Insights / Analytics.

Intended outcomes. Shorter perceived wait times, better-informed conversations with staff, 1 experience across online and store, and conversion and retention that can be measured in the platform's reports.

Use case 2: first-party data targeting for retail media

Uses loyalty and other proprietary data to target in-store campaigns as third-party cookies decline.

Automatic store check-in

  • Juniper MIST virtual-BLE access points detect a customer's phone through your retailer app and check them in automatically. See Enable proximity personalisation with MIST.
  • A push notification greets the customer on arrival.
  • The customer's proximity to a zone or virtual beacon decides what nearby signage shows.

Connected customer journeys

  • Unified profiles personalise digital signage and tablets. See Trigger campaigns from customer or decisioning data.
  • Content targets the customer's location or the aggregated behaviour of a store section.
  • First-party cookies personalise displays for unknown prospects.

QR code store check-in

  • Dynamic QR codes on signage enable check-in and surface loyalty data. See Enable QR Control and set the default QR code settings.
  • QR Control campaigns let customers browse personalised offers and play content on the screen.
  • Experiences adapt to the aisle or zone through zone-specific mobile site templates. See Personalise a visitor's store experience.

Programmatic advertising slots (coming soon)

Localised, personalised and sponsored ad slots that a brand designates for advertisers, bookable in advance or filled programmatically, with DSP integrations planned. This capability is on the roadmap and is not in the platform today.

Intended outcomes. Larger baskets and higher conversion, monetisation of in-store media, closed-loop attribution through the Downloads reports, and the ability to change a campaign in real time. See Review campaign performance in Insights / Analytics.

Use case 3: hyper-localised campaigns for quick-service restaurants

Quick-service restaurants integrate local data to control how menus and offers are presented.

Day-parting (advanced scheduling)

  • Schedule breakfast, lunch and dinner menus by time of day, or only while the store is open. See Schedule a campaign.
  • Targeting rules refine which menu each store or screen shows. See Target a campaign.

Dynamic data integration

  • Adapt offers to local weather with Hot Day and Cold Day store segments — soups on cold days, cold drinks on hot days. See Localise campaigns with store segments.
  • Hide sold-out items by switching an out-of-stock segment on from the staff tablet. See Update your store's segments (Retail Admin).

Personalised offers

  • A QR code scan retrieves the customer's profile and prior orders through the Visitor API. See Connect your mobile app or third-party system to the Visitor API.
  • Loyalty and behavioural data unlock personalised discounts on the mobile store site.

Vision at the edge (audience sensing)

  • Estimate the gender and age range of passers-by and target campaigns accordingly. See Target passers-by using computer vision at the edge.
  • Monitor real-world campaign performance and optimise it with closed-loop campaign monitoring. See Configure campaign playback monitoring.
  • The complexity of the vision model depends on the player hardware. See Does computer vision store images of shoppers?.

Intended outcomes. Higher sales per visit, less manual menu maintenance, more engagement with offers, campaign decisions based on playback and audience data, and less waste from promoting items that are out of stock.
